description: Radiation-risk activities per 38 CFR Part 3. A 'radiation-exposed veteran' is one who participated in a radiation-risk activity as defined in §3.309(d)(3)(ii).

operations.name: Occupation of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
operations.description: Service in a capacity which, if combatant, entitled the veteran to receive the Combat Infantryman Badge or equivalent badge, or occupational forces of Hiroshima/Nagasaki during the period August 6, 1945 through July 1, 1946.

operations.name: Internment as POW in Japan (Proximity to Hiroshima/Nagasaki)
operations.description: Internment as a prisoner of war in Japan (or service on combatant or non-combatant ships present in Hiroshima or Nagasaki harbors) during the period Aug 6, 1945 - Jul 1, 1946.

operations.name: Operation TRINITY
operations.description: First nuclear device detonation, Alamogordo, New Mexico. On-site test participation.

operations.name: Operation CROSSROADS
operations.description: Atmospheric nuclear weapons tests at Bikini Atoll, Marshall Islands. Tests ABLE and BAKER.

operations.name: Operation SANDSTONE
operations.description: Atmospheric nuclear weapons tests at Enewetak Atoll, Marshall Islands.

operations.name: Operation RANGER
operations.description: Atmospheric nuclear weapons tests at Nevada Test Site.

operations.name: Operation GREENHOUSE
operations.description: Atmospheric nuclear weapons tests at Enewetak Atoll, Marshall Islands.

operations.name: Operation BUSTER-JANGLE
operations.description: Atmospheric nuclear weapons tests at Nevada Test Site.

operations.name: Operation TUMBLER-SNAPPER
operations.description: Atmospheric nuclear weapons tests at Nevada Test Site.

operations.name: Operation IVY
operations.description: Atmospheric nuclear weapons tests at Enewetak Atoll including first thermonuclear device (Mike shot).

operations.name: Operation UPSHOT-KNOTHOLE
operations.description: Atmospheric nuclear weapons tests at Nevada Test Site. 11 detonations including Grable atomic artillery test.

operations.name: Operation CASTLE
operations.description: Atmospheric nuclear weapons tests at Bikini and Enewetak Atolls. Included Bravo shot, the largest US nuclear test (15 megatons).

operations.name: Operation TEAPOT
operations.description: Atmospheric nuclear weapons tests at Nevada Test Site. 14 detonations.

operations.name: Operation WIGWAM
operations.description: Deep underwater nuclear test approximately 500 miles southwest of San Diego, CA.
operations.location: Pacific Ocean (500 mi SW of San Diego)

operations.name: Operation REDWING
operations.description: Atmospheric nuclear weapons tests at Bikini and Enewetak Atolls. 17 detonations.

operations.name: Operation PLUMBBOB
operations.description: Atmospheric nuclear weapons tests at Nevada Test Site. 29 detonations including first underground nuclear test.

operations.name: Operation HARDTACK I
operations.description: Atmospheric nuclear weapons tests at Bikini and Enewetak Atolls, and Johnston Island. 35 detonations.
operations.location: Pacific Proving Grounds (Bikini, Enewetak, Johnston Island)

operations.name: Operation ARGUS
operations.description: High-altitude nuclear tests over the South Atlantic Ocean. Three detonations launched from USS Norton Sound.

operations.name: Operation HARDTACK II
operations.description: Nuclear weapons tests at Nevada Test Site. 37 detonations, last atmospheric tests before moratorium.

operations.name: Operation NOUGAT
operations.description: Underground nuclear tests at Nevada Test Site. First series after testing moratorium.

operations.name: Operation DOMINIC I
operations.description: Atmospheric nuclear weapons tests at Christmas Island and Johnston Island. 36 detonations, last US atmospheric test series.

operations.name: Operation DOMINIC II / STORAX
operations.description: Underground nuclear tests at Nevada Test Site conducted as part of the 1962 test series.

operations.name: Project PLOWSHARE (Peaceful Nuclear Explosions)
operations.description: Peaceful nuclear explosions program including tests such as SEDAN, GNOME, and GASBUGGY. Service members who participated in or were present at these detonations.
operations.location: Various US Sites (NTS, Carlsbad NM, Farmington NM)

operations.name: Palomares, Spain Nuclear Accident Cleanup
operations.description: Cleanup of radioactive contamination from B-52/KC-135 mid-air collision near Palomares, Spain that released four thermonuclear weapons.

operations.name: Thule, Greenland Nuclear Accident Response
operations.description: Response and cleanup following B-52 crash carrying thermonuclear weapons near Thule Air Base, Greenland.

operations.name: Enewetak Atoll Radiological Cleanup
operations.description: Radiological cleanup of Enewetak Atoll in the Marshall Islands. Approximately 6,000 service members participated.

operations.name: Underground Nuclear Tests (Nevada Test Site / NNSS)
operations.description: Participation in underground nuclear testing at the Nevada Test Site (now Nevada National Security Site). Per §3.311, veterans who participated in aboveground or underground nuclear testing may be eligible for radiogenic disease claims.

operations.name: Operations LONGSHOT, MILROW, and CANNIKIN (Amchitka Island)
operations.description: Underground nuclear tests conducted on Amchitka Island, Alaska. Three tests: LONGSHOT (1965), MILROW (1969), and CANNIKIN (1971).

operations.name: Project VELA (Nuclear Test Detection)
operations.description: Service members who participated in the VELA satellite and surface detection program for monitoring nuclear detonations, potentially with exposure to radiation sources.

operations.name: Nuclear-Powered Warship/Submarine Overhaul (Shipyard Workers)
operations.description: Service members exposed to ionizing radiation during nuclear-powered warship or submarine overhaul at naval shipyards (Portsmouth, Norfolk, Pearl Harbor, Puget Sound, Mare Island, etc.). Dose reconstruction available via Navy dosimetry records.

operations.name: DTRA Radiation Dose Reconstruction (Other Confirmed Exposures)
operations.description: Any other service member whose occupational exposure to ionizing radiation is confirmed through DTRA (Defense Threat Reduction Agency) dose reconstruction records. This is a catch-all for veterans with confirmed radiation exposure not otherwise listed.

presumptiveConditions_309d.description: Diseases specific to radiation-exposed veterans. Service connection is presumptive if disease manifests in a radiation-exposed veteran.
conditions: Primary liver cancer (except if cirrhosis or hepatitis B indicated)

radiogenicDiseases_311.description: Radiogenic diseases for which dose assessment and advisory opinion may be obtained under §3.311. These are NOT automatically presumptive — they require dose reconstruction and medical opinion.
conditions: All forms of leukemia except chronic lymphocytic leukemia
Tumors of the brain and central nervous system
